sourceEvidence.claim: Azoles — the single-line drug roster (the chapter's longest)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Azoles

Clotrimazole, fluconazole, isavuconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, miconazole, voriconazole.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Azoles — MECHANISM (the lanosterol→ergosterol P-450)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM

Inhibit fungal sterol (ergosterol) synthesis by inhibiting the cytochrome P-450 enzyme that converts
lanosterol to ergosterol.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Azoles — CLINICAL USE (the site-by-site azole routing)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Local and less serious systemic mycoses. Fluconazole for chronic suppression of cryptococcal
meningitis in people living with HIV and candidal infections of all types. Itraconazole may
be used for Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Histoplasma, Sporothrix schenckii. Clotrimazole and
miconazole for topical fungal infections. Voriconazole for Aspergillus and some Candida.
Isavuconazole for serious Aspergillus and Mucor infections.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Azoles — ADVERSE EFFECTS (gynecomastia esp. ketoconazole; P-450; QT)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Testosterone synthesis inhibition (gynecomastia, especially with ketoconazole), liver dysfunction
(inhibits cytochrome P-450), QT interval prolongation.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Terbinafine — MECHANISM + CLINICAL USE + ADVERSE
sourceEvidence.quote:
Terbinafine
MECHANISM

Inhibits the fungal enzyme squalene epoxidase.

CLINICAL USE

Dermatophytoses (especially onychomycosis—fungal infection of finger or toe nails).

ADVERSE EFFECTS

GI upset, headaches, hepatotoxicity, taste disturbance.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Echinocandins — the full card (anidulafungin, caspofungin, micafungin; β-glucan)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Echinocandins

Anidulafungin, caspofungin, micafungin.

MECHANISM

Inhibit cell wall synthesis by inhibiting synthesis of β-glucan.

CLINICAL USE

Invasive aspergillosis, Candida.

ADVERSE EFFECTS

GI upset, flushing (by histamine release).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Griseofulvin — the full card (microtubules; keratin; disulfiram-like; ↑warfarin)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Griseofulvin
MECHANISM

Interferes with microtubule function; disrupts mitosis. Deposits in keratin-containing tissues (eg,
nails).

CLINICAL USE

Oral treatment of superficial infections; inhibits growth of dermatophytes (tinea, ringworm).

ADVERSE EFFECTS

Teratogenic, carcinogenic, confusion, headaches, disulfiram-like reaction, ↑ cytochrome P-450 and
warfarin metabolism.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The antiprotozoal tail block (pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine through stibogluconate)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Antiprotozoal therapy

Pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine (toxoplasmosis), suramin and melarsoprol (Trypanosoma brucei),
nifurtimox (T cruzi), sodium stibogluconate (leishmaniasis).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The anti-mite/louse tail block (permethrin, malathion, ivermectin)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Anti-mite/louse
therapy

Permethrin, malathion (acetylcholinesterase inhibitor), topical or oral ivermectin. Used to treat
scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) and lice (Pediculus and Pthirus).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Chloroquine — MECHANISM + CLINICAL USE (heme→hemozoin; non-falciparum)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Chloroquine
MECHANISM

Blocks detoxification of heme into hemozoin. Heme accumulates and is toxic to plasmodia.

CLINICAL USE

Treatment of plasmodial species other than P falciparum (due to drug resistance from membrane
pump that ↓ intracellular concentration of drug).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Chloroquine — ADVERSE EFFECTS (cumulative-dose retinopathy; pruritus)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Retinopathy (dependent on cumulative dose); pruritus (especially in dark-skinned individuals).
